title: Non-blocking follow-ups from PR #112 review (frontend-oscillator-chart-followups)
description: Non-blocking findings from pr-reviewer's review of PR #112 (frontend-oscillator-chart-followups), recorded here so they aren't lost once that PR merges. The blocking finding -- schemas.py's stochastic_k Field description (and its copies in openapi.json/types.ts/OscillatorChart.tsx) claiming a '~11 prior bars' warm-up window when the actual warm-up (per app/indicators/stochastic.py's own docstring math, k_period-1+smooth-1=4+2=6, and confirmed by this PR's own new test asserting points[:6] are null) is 6 -- is tracked as the needs_work verdict on the parent task itself, not here.

checklist.step: docs/architecture/API.md's `GET /api/stocks/{ticker}/indicators` section (example JSON + prose, around lines 66-93) was not updated by PR #112 to mention that stochastic_k/force_index_2ema can legitimately be null for a bar still inside its indicator's warm-up window -- the example payload only shows non-null values and the prose is silent on this, even though backend/app/api/schemas.py's IndicatorHistoryPoint was widened to float | None specifically for this reason. Update the doc (prose note + optionally a second example point showing a null) to match the current, accurate contract.

GET /api/stocks/{ticker}/indicators?range=max is very slow against the live (non-fixture) data provider for a long-lived ticker: observed >120s and climbing CPU-bound single-request time for AAPL (whose real history goes back to 1980), since the endpoint re-runs the full per-bar Triple Screen signal engine (analyse_history) once per daily bar in the requested range with no caching of the computed per-bar results -- OHLCV itself is cached (app/data/cache.py) but the derived signal/indicator history is recomputed from scratch on every request. Pre-existing behavior, not introduced by PR #112's diff (backend/app/api/routers/stocks.py is unchanged in that PR) -- surfaced incidentally while doing PR #112's required browser walkthrough of the Max range case (which had to be re-run against FINTRADE_DATA_PROVIDER_MODE=fixture to get a usable response time). Worth profiling/caching analyse_history's per-bar output, or at least documenting the expected latency for a 'max' range on a decades-old ticker.
